title: Affordances from Human Videos as a Versatile Representation for Robotics
tldr: Predict where and how a human would interact from internet video, and that single affordance map slots into imitation, exploration, goal-conditioned learning and RL alike.

problem.task: Learn a visual affordance model from human video and use it as the interface to four different robot learning paradigms.

inputs.name: scene image
inputs.chars: From the robot's camera, in unmodified real environments.

outputs.name: post-contact trajectory
outputs.chars: How the interaction would proceed, which is the half a contact point alone leaves out.

training.supervision: Human hand trajectories extracted from internet videos of people acting in environments.
training.note: Environment-centric rather than hand-centric framing is what makes the output usable by a robot with different kinematics.

method.intuition: Human video cannot be imitated joint-for-joint, but the where-and-how of interaction transfers, and that is enough to seed four kinds of robot learning.
components: contact point and post-contact trajectory prediction
integration with offline imitation, exploration, goal-conditioned learning and RL

experiments.headline: Effective across 4 real-world environments, over 10 tasks and 2 robot platforms operating in the wild.

why: The cleanest formulation of what transfers from human video to robot action: the affordance rather than the motion.

title: Being-H0: Vision-Language-Action Pretraining from Large-Scale Human Videos
tldr: Treat the human hand as the foundation manipulator: tokenize hand motion at part level to millimetre accuracy and pretrain a VLA on web video before it ever sees a robot.

problem.task: Dexterous VLA pretraining on human hand motion, then adaptation to robot hands.

outputs.name: hand motion tokens
outputs.chars: Part-level tokenization reconstructing hand trajectories to millimetre accuracy; retargeted to robot hands after post-training.

training.supervision: Physical instruction tuning: large-scale VLA pretraining on human video, physical space alignment for 3D, then robot post-training.
training.note: The curation pipeline unifies motion capture, VR and RGB-only sources into millions of motion-based instruction instances.

method.intuition: The scale and diversity bottleneck in robot learning disappears if the manipulator you pretrain on is the one already filmed a billion times.

datasets.name: curated human hand motion corpus (millions of instances)

baselines: VLAs pretrained on synthetic or teleoperated data
experiments.headline: Scales with model and data size, with gains on real-world robotic manipulation carried over from human-video pretraining.

why: The strongest version of the argument that the human-embodiment and robot-embodiment branches share a training corpus.

title: EgoVLA: Learning Vision-Language-Action Models from Egocentric Human Videos
tldr: Predict human wrist and hand actions from egocentric video, then IK-retarget to a humanoid — robot hardware only enters at fine-tuning time.

problem.task: Train a VLA on human egocentric video, retarget to a bimanual humanoid, fine-tune on a few robot demonstrations.

inputs.name: egocentric frames
inputs.chars: First-person, diverse scenes and tasks — the reason for using human data.

outputs.name: wrist + hand action
outputs.chars: Human action space; converted to robot joints by inverse kinematics and retargeting.

training.supervision: Human egocentric video for pretraining, a small set of robot demonstrations for fine-tuning.
training.note: A purpose-built simulation benchmark supplies the bimanual evaluation the human data cannot.

method.intuition: Robot hardware caps how much data you can collect, so put the hardware only at the end of the pipeline and let human video carry the scale.
components: human wrist and hand action prediction

experiments.headline: Significant improvements over baselines, with ablations isolating how much the human data contributes.

why: The most direct pipeline from the egocentric datasets in this list to a robot policy.

title: DexUMI: Using Human Hand as the Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Manipulation
tldr: Close the embodiment gap physically with a hand exoskeleton and visually by inpainting the robot hand over the human one. The human demonstration is then already robot data.

problem.task: Collect dexterous demonstrations with a human hand and train a policy for a robot hand directly on them.

inputs.name: wrist-camera video
inputs.chars: Recorded during human demonstration; the human hand is replaced by an inpainted robot hand.

outputs.name: robot hand action
outputs.chars: Directly executable — the exoskeleton constrained the human motion to be feasible.

training.supervision: Behavior cloning on the adapted demonstrations.
training.note: Two gaps are closed by two different means: kinematics by hardware, appearance by inpainting.

method.intuition: Remove the human-robot embodiment gap instead of learning to bridge it: physically with an exoskeleton, visually with inpainting.
components: wearable hand exoskeleton with haptic feedback
policy learning on two robot hand platforms

experiments.headline: 86% average task success across real-world experiments on two different dexterous hand platforms.

why: The human hand as an interface rather than as a source of imitation — an underrated third option between teleoperation and video.

title: TWIST: Teleoperated Whole-Body Imitation System
tldr: One controller for the whole humanoid body driven by a person's motion, so locomotion and manipulation stop being separate systems.

problem.task: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation by motion imitation.

inputs.name: human motion
inputs.chars: Retargeted to the humanoid's kinematics; the operator's body is the interface.

outputs.name: whole-body joint targets
outputs.chars: One unified network for locomotion, manipulation and expressive motion.

training.supervision: RL plus behavior cloning against retargeted mocap reference clips.
training.note: Privileged future motion frames and real-world mocap both measurably improve tracking, which is the analysis the paper contributes.

method.intuition: Human motion is the most natural interface for a humanoid because the degrees of freedom already correspond, if the controller can track them robustly enough.

experiments.headline: Coordinated whole-body skills — whole-body manipulation, legged manipulation, locomotion and expressive movement — from one unified controller.

why: The human-and-robot pairing at its tightest: the person is the policy and the robot is the body.

title: Multi-agent Long-term 3D Human Pose Forecasting via Interaction-aware Trajectory Conditioning
tldr: Forecast where everyone is going first, then condition each body's pose on its own trajectory mode. Coarse-to-fine is what makes 6 s horizons and 5+ agents tractable.

outputs.name: local poses
outputs.chars: Conditioned on each trajectory mode; horizons beyond 6 s.

training.supervision: Supervised forecasting. A new long-horizon multi-agent set is built from real images and 2D annotations to make 6 s and 5+ agents evaluable at all.
training.note: The dataset gap is the reason long-horizon multi-agent forecasting was under-measured.

method.intuition: Pose and trajectory are coupled, because where you are going shapes how you move. So forecast the coarse trajectory first and let it condition the fine pose.

experiments.headline: State-of-the-art prediction on both the new complex dataset and simpler existing ones.

why: The perception layer a robot needs before it can share a workspace with people — forecasting is what makes collaboration safe.

title: Spot-On: A Mixed Reality Interface for Multi-Robot Cooperation
tldr: Mixed reality as the control surface for a team of quadrupeds working on drawers, doors and light switches in a real building.

problem.task: Let one person direct multiple legged robots through semantically diverse environments from a mixed-reality interface.

inputs.name: user selection in MR
inputs.chars: Pointed at directly in the room rather than typed.

inputs.name: robot state and scene
inputs.chars: Shared between robots and the headset.

outputs.name: robot task assignment
outputs.chars: Includes articulated objects — drawers, swing doors — and building infrastructure like light switches.

training.supervision: None — a systems contribution evaluated by user study.
training.note: The interesting part is which decisions stay with the person and which go to the robots.

method.intuition: Coordinating several robots in a real building is an interface problem before it is a planning problem.

experiments.headline: Participants rated design and usability "good" or "very good" in almost all cases.

why: The human-and-robot branch as an interaction problem, which is where most of it actually lives.

title: Reality Proxy: Fluid Interactions with Real-World Objects in MR via Abstract Representations
tldr: Selecting a physical object in MR is hard because physics gets in the way. Hand the user an AI-enriched abstract proxy and filtering, grouping and multi-select become easy.

problem.task: Select and manipulate real-world objects in mixed reality when they are crowded, distant or occluded.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.chars: MR passthrough of a real environment.

inputs.name: user gesture
inputs.chars: Standard gestures — no new vocabulary introduced.

outputs.name: proxy interaction
outputs.chars: Proxies carry AI-derived semantic attributes and hierarchical spatial relationships.

training.supervision: None — an interaction technique evaluated by expert review.
training.note: Decoupling interaction from physical constraints is the general move. The AI enrichment is what makes the proxies more than icons.

method.intuition: Interaction difficulty comes from acting on physical objects under their physical constraints. Shift the target to a representation and the constraints go away.

datasets.name: office retrieval, large-scale navigation, multi-drone control scenarios

metrics: expert evaluation of utility and usability
experiments.headline: Enables interactions that are cumbersome or impossible with direct manipulation, without new gestures or menus.

why: A reminder that the interface between a person and the physical world is itself a representation choice.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
tldr: Interleave a thought and an action in the same token stream, feed the observation back in, repeat. The loop pattern almost every embodied agent now uses.

problem.task: Interleaved reasoning and acting in a text-based environment loop.

inputs.name: observation
inputs.chars: Returned by the environment after each action and appended to the context.

outputs.name: thought
outputs.chars: Free-form reasoning that updates the plan without touching the world.

training.note: Reasoning-only hallucinates because nothing corrects it. Acting-only cannot revise because it never reflects. The interleaving is the whole contribution.

method.intuition: Thinking without acting drifts from reality and acting without thinking cannot recover from a mistake, so alternate them in one stream.

experiments.headline: +34% absolute success on ALFWorld and +10% on WebShop over imitation and reinforcement learning baselines, with fewer hallucinations than reasoning-only prompting.

why: The loop this list is organized around, written down in its most compressed form, and the reason to ask why physical loops rarely look this clean.

title: Vesta: A Generalist Embodied Reasoning Model
tldr: One model for localization, spatial reasoning, navigation and long-horizon planning beats an oracle ensemble that picks the best specialist for every category.

problem.task: Unified embodied reasoning: grounding, navigation, embodied QA and long-horizon planning in one model.

inputs.name: memory
inputs.chars: Retained history frames interleaved with a running text log of finished subtasks — no learned memory module.

outputs.name: reasoned decision
outputs.chars: Grounding, navigation target or next subtask.

training.supervision: Curated SFT corpus mixing grounding, navigation, embodied QA and real-robot data.
training.note: The memory harness is deliberately simple, which strengthens the claim that the corpus is doing the work.

method.intuition: A stack of specialists behind a planner pays latency for every hop and lets one bad output cascade. A single generalist removes both failure modes, if the data mixture is right.

experiments.headline: Beats individual SOTA baselines by >20% on average and an oracle ensemble by >10%, with >35% higher success on memory-heavy long-horizon real robot tasks.

why: The current strongest evidence that the specialist-stack architecture of embodied AI is being replaced by one model.

title: BEHAVIOR-1K: A Human-Centered, Embodied AI Benchmark with 1,000 Everyday Activities and Realistic Simulation
tldr: The task list came from asking people what they actually want a robot to do, and the simulator handles the rigid bodies, deformables and liquids those answers imply.

problem.task: Long-horizon everyday household activities in realistic simulation, with sim-to-real calibration.

inputs.name: simulated observation
inputs.chars: From OMNIGIBSON, with rigid bodies, deformables and liquids.

inputs.name: activity definition
inputs.chars: Defined over object physical and semantic properties, not over trajectories.

training.note: Defining success as a logical goal state rather than a trajectory is what lets 1,000 activities be scored consistently.

method.intuition: Benchmarks drift toward what is easy to simulate. Grounding the task list in a survey of what people want keeps it pointed at reality.

experiments.headline: Activities are long-horizon and manipulation-heavy enough to remain unsolved by current methods. An initial mobile-manipulator sim-to-real transfer study calibrates the gap.

why: Anchors the change arc in what people actually want changed, which is the question the whole field is downstream of.

title: RoboCasa: Large-Scale Simulation of Everyday Tasks for Generalist Robots
tldr: Uses generative models to populate the simulator — text-to-3D objects, text-to-image textures, LLM-composed tasks — so scale comes from generation rather than collection.

problem.task: Large-scale simulated kitchen manipulation for training and evaluating generalist policies.

inputs.name: simulated observation
inputs.chars: Kitchen scenes, 150+ object categories, interactable furniture and appliances.

training.supervision: Human demonstrations plus automated trajectory generation that multiplies them.
training.note: The scaling study on synthetic data is the result most often cited from this paper.

method.intuition: Robot data is scarce because environments are scarce, and generative models can manufacture environments faster than people can build them.
components: thousands of generated 3D assets across 150+ categories

metrics: imitation learning success vs. dataset size
experiments.headline: A clear scaling trend from synthetically generated robot data, with evidence of transfer to real-world tasks.

why: The other answer to the data bottleneck: generate the world instead of recording it.
